The Accessibility toggle turns itself off

By far the most common issue. On Android 13+, the system blocks sideloaded apps from turning Accessibility on through the normal toggle, as a security measure — if it switches back off right after you enable it, this is why, not a bug.

Fix: open the app's info screen below, tap the three-dot menu (or look for the option directly), and enable "Allow restricted setting". Then try the Accessibility toggle again.

If your device doesn't show that option at all, you'll need a one-time ADB command from a computer or phone (atvTools app) — see the full install guide below for the exact steps.
Nothing happens when I click a recommendation

Check, in order: 1) The Accessibility toggle is actually ON — reopen Accessibility settings and confirm it didn\'t silently switch off (see above). 2) Your chosen destination app (Nuvio, Stremio, Plex, Jellyfin, WuPlay…) is installed and up to date. 3) Not every recommendation card exposes a title — small banners and ads are skipped on purpose, that\'s expected.

Voice search is a separate, optional toggle from the main Accessibility service. Go back to the main screen and make sure you\'ve also tapped \"Enable voice search\" and granted the one-time screen recording permission it asks for — enabling only the main service isn\'t enough for voice search to work.
On Fire TV, nothing seems to work at all

Fire OS blocks the standard Accessibility method for sideloaded apps entirely — no setting fixes that. On Fire TV you need \"Fire TV mode\" instead (the button on the main screen changes automatically once it detects Fire TV). It needs \"Usage access\" granted first — use the button below — then a one-time screen recording permission.
The full visual install guide has screenshots for every step above, including the exact ADB/atvTools commands for the Restricted Settings fix.
